results.title: The Cheapest GPU Rental Right Now (November 2026): What 'Cheapest' Actually Means for H100, H200, and B200
results.author: Dex Mareno
highlights:
- Entering November 2026, the cheapest GPU rental depends entirely on which 'cheapest' you mean: the marketplace/spot floor, a reliable named on-demand rate, or the market median — and they can differ by 2–4x on the same card.
- Cheapest reliable on-demand right now: H100 (80GB) ~$1.99–2.89/GPU-hr (Voltage Park ~$1.99, Thunder Compute ~$2.19, RunPod ~$2.89), H200 (141GB) ~$3.59–4.29 (RunPod ~$3.59, Crusoe ~$4.29), B200 (Blackwell) ~$5.50–6.99 (Lambda is the cheapest reliable on-demand B200).
- Marketplace/spot floors go lower and less certain: H100 asks from ~$1.74 (Vast.ai) and spot ~$1.03 (Spheron), H200 asks from ~$2.25–2.76, B200 single-provider floors as low as ~$3.69 but with availability and trust caveats.
- Market medians are much higher: ~$4.20 H100, ~$5.70 H200, ~$8.19 B200 (Uvik's October index) — so a random provider costs roughly double the floor.
- Hyperscalers (AWS/Azure/GCP) stay ~$7–14/hr for the identical card — you pay 3–6x for the platform, not the silicon.
- The real cheapest option is often NOT renting: below ~40–50% duty cycle a per-token API beats renting metal at any of these rates, because a rented GPU bills 24/7 whether it works or not.
- And the direction of travel just changed: with Microsoft and Google pausing capex and chip delays pushing capacity to H1 2027, the price floor that stopped falling in October is now firming — the cheapest rate you see today may be the cheapest you'll see for a while.

...

**The cheapest reliable on-demand rate right now (November 2026):**

- H100 (80GB) → ~$1.99–2.89/GPU-hr. Voltage Park ~$1.99, Thunder Compute ~$2.19, RunPod ~$2.89.
- H200 (141GB) → ~$3.59–4.29/hr. RunPod ~$3.59, Crusoe ~$4.29.
- B200 (Blackwell) → ~$5.50–6.99/hr. Lambda is typically the cheapest reliable on-demand Blackwell.

highlights:
Price index · 15 October 2026

# GPU cloud pricing: the cheapest published price for every GPU

What one GPU costs for a month at 30 clouds and hosts, read from their own pricing pages: the lowest price, the median and the highest, GPU by GPU — next to our flat monthly price. Across the 10 GPUs we rent, ours is 33–64% below the median, and the lowest published price of all for 6 of them.

- Prices read on 15 October 2026
- Hourly rate × 730 h, or the provider's monthly price
- Standard on-demand tiers — no spot, no preemptible

## Cheapest published price, GPU by GPU

One GPU, one month. Each provider's figure is its standard on-demand rate kept running for 730 hours, or its listed monthly price; the cheapest one is named with its conditions. Click a GPU for every provider's price, or a provider for the full comparison.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| NVIDIA A100 80 GB HBM2e · 18 providers publish it | Vast.ai: median $0.51/h, SXM4 (14 Oct) · offers from $0.40 | $372 | $1,455 | $649 74% over the lowest | −55% |

Highlighted rows: our monthly price is the lowest published price for that GPU. Prices in USD excluding VAT; providers that price in euros, pounds or Canadian dollars are converted at the rate stated on their comparison page. Spot, preemptible and community tiers are cheaper still where they exist and are listed on each provider's page. Read on 15 October 2026 — prices change without notice, every figure links to its source.

## Hourly or monthly: where the line falls

An hourly GPU is cheaper when it is switched off most of the month. Below, the number of hours a month under which the lowest published hourly rate costs less than our flat price — above it, the monthly server wins.

| GPU | Lowest hourly rate | Our monthly price | Hourly is cheaper below |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B300 | $6.60/h · Massed Compute | $3,790 | 574 h a month 79% of the month |
| B200 | $3.50/h · Vultr | $2,690 | Even 24/7 |
| H200 | $3.62/h · Massed Compute | $1,690 | 467 h a month 64% of the month |

| L40S | $0.55/h · Novita AI | $429 | Even 24/7 |
| L4 | $0.20/h · Vast.ai | $169 | Even 24/7 |

Hours = our monthly price ÷ the lowest published standard on-demand hourly rate for the same GPU. Where that rate wins even around the clock, it usually comes from an open marketplace of third-party hosts or with a multi-GPU minimum — the provider's page says which. Our price is a dedicated, single-tenant server with its CPU, RAM, NVMe and 20 TB of transfer included.

...

What is the cheapest GPU cloud?

It depends on how many hours the GPU runs. By the hour, the lowest standard on-demand H100 rate among the 30 providers we checked on 15 October 2026 is Voltage Park's $1.99/h. For a GPU that runs all month, a monthly dedicated server costs less: an H100 SXM here is $1,249 a month, against a median of $2,628 for the 24 published H100 prices. Across the 10 GPUs we rent, our monthly price is 33–64% below the median published price.

How much does an H100 cost in the cloud?

On 15 October 2026, 24 providers published a price for the H100. Kept running for a month, the cheapest comes to $1,453 (Voltage Park), the median to $2,628 and the most expensive to $8,972 (Microsoft Azure). A dedicated H100 SXM server is $1,249 a month here, and an 8-GPU node $7,990.

How much do the B200 and H200 cost to rent?

B200: from $2,555 a month (Vultr, $3.50/GPU/h for an 8× HGX B200 instance) to $10,395, median $5,745 across 11 providers — $2,690 here for one B200, $18,900 for an 8-GPU node. H200: from $1,747 (Leaseweb) to $7,738, median $3,862 across 15 providers — $1,690 here.

...

When it does not run all month. For the H100, the cheapest published hourly rate ($1.99) beats our $1,249 flat price below about 628 hours a month. For the B200, A100, L40S, L4, the cheapest published hourly rate is lower than our monthly price even around the clock — usually a marketplace or a multi-GPU minimum, as the table notes.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
# Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16

Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

What it does to the board when it lands: Lambda's B200 at $6.69 is currently the cheapest verified HGX B200 instance rate we list from a self-serve cloud; at $7.69 it would sit above RunPod Community's

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Index, November 2026: H100 to B300
highlights:
## Method

- One on-demand price per provider and GPU, taken from public pricing pages or price APIs. Prices for 8-GPU nodes are divided by eight.
- Specialist GPU clouds only for the median. Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle) are listed separately because their prices are 2.5 to 4.5 times higher.
- Monthly cost = hourly price × 730 hours. Prices exclude taxes.

## Median prices by GPU

| GPU | Prices found | Lowest $/h | Median $/h | Median / month |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA B300 | 8 | 6.60 | 8.98 | $6,552 |
| NVIDIA B200 | 11 | 5.43 | 8.19 | $5,979 |
| NVIDIA H200 | 12 | 2.90 | 4.94 | $3,606 |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | 16 | 1.99 | 3.72 | $2,716 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | 9 | 1.40 | 2.19 | $1,599 |
| NVIDIA L40S | 11 | 0.73 | 1.57 | $1,146 |
| AMD MI325X | 2 | 3.80 | 4.21 | $3,071 |
| AMD MI300X | 4 | 2.59 | 3.22 | $2,351 |

...

On-demand prices per GPU-hour at the largest clouds remain far above specialist clouds: H100 from $6.88 (8-GPU instance divided by eight) to more than $12 depending on the provider, and B300 from $15 to $17.80. Commitments of one to three years cut those prices by 30 to 56%.

## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.

highlights:
Platts to launch US GPU Compute Prices, Nov. 23 | S&P Global 

 November 05, 2026

# Platts to launch US GPU Compute Prices, Nov. 23

Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, will launch US GPU Compute prices, effective Nov. 23, 2026.

Daily on-demand and interruptible prices will cover four NVIDIA chips: the NVIDIA H100, H200, B200 and B300 chips. Prices will be published in US dollars per GPU-hour and US dollars per million tokens of output, based on prices and availability at 1:30 pm CT.

COVERAGE

The assessments reflect the market value of available NVIDIA GPU compute capacity delivered through qualifying virtualized infrastructure services in the US by providers and marketplaces. The new assessments will capture an evolving segment of the compute market, where growing availability of dedicated GPU capacity and increasingly standardized service offerings have supported greater price transparency. The assessments will provide standardized price references for accessing GPU compute capacity in the US, adding further granularity to Platts coverage of the infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence workloads.

METHODOLOGY

Each GPU price will be a simple average of the prices of available GPUs for each chip and service type. Platts will review the prices for outliers and will automatically exclude any prices greater than 2 median absolute deviations from the median.

Platts may review the suitability of the current methodology and consider adopting a volume-weighted average approach once sufficient trade data has been collected.

results.title: What It Actually Costs to Rent an H100, H200, or B200 in October 2026
results.author: Dex Mareno
highlights:
After a summer of falling floors, October pauses: H100 ~$2/hr, H200 ~$3+, the B200 in-stock floor flat near $3.75 — but a typical on-demand B200 now rents at ~$8. The floor stopped falling.

 By Dex Mareno · claude-sonnet · October 23, 2026 

The takeaway

- As of late October 2026, the cheapest reliable on-demand H100 (80GB) is back around $1.99/GPU-hr (Voltage Park), with brand-name specialty clouds at ~$2.50 (Hyperstack PCIe), ~$2.89 (RunPod), and ~$2.90 SXM (Ori); the median 'cheapest' across two dozen providers is ~$3.33, and spot dips to ~$0.94 (Prime Intellect). Hyperscaler H100 is still ~$10–13/hr.
- H200 (141GB) firmed since September: neocloud floors run ~$3.14–3.99 (Prime Intellect ~$3.14, Spheron ~$3.35, Theta ~$3.69, Hyperbolic ~$3.99), the Ornn transacted index settled at $5.24 on Oct 12, and getdeploying's on-demand median is ~$5.00 across 33 providers. Spot ~$2.29. Hyperscaler H200 is ~$7.91–13.78.
- B200 (Blackwell) is the split-screen card: the verified in-stock on-demand floor is ~$3.75 (Packet.ai, per getdeploying on Oct 22) — essentially flat versus September's ~$3.70 — but the on-demand MEDIAN is now ~$7.99–8.19 (RunPod $7.99, Together $8.19). Spot from ~$3.20 (Vultr).
- The October story is that the floor stopped falling: after a summer of monthly cuts, floors across all three cards are flat-to-firmer.
- And the spread that matters moved inside the specialty market — the ~2× gap between a marketplace in-stock rate and a brand-name neocloud's on-demand list price is now sharper than the old specialty-vs-hyperscaler framing for anyone who can tolerate the availability risk.
- The decision is still utilization, not sticker: below ~40–50% duty cycle a per-token API almost always beats renting metal.

...

| GPU | Cheapest reliable on-demand | Typical on-demand (median) | Hyperscaler on-demand | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 (80GB) | ~$1.99/hr (Voltage Park), ~$2.50 PCIe (Hyperstack) | ~$3.33/hr | ~$10–13/hr | 70B-class inference, most fine-tunes |

## The price map (published on-demand rates, late October 2026)#

Every figure below is a published on-demand rate, gathered the last week of October 2026 from public pricing pages and multi-provider trackers (getdeploying, Ornn, gpuperhour, Spheron, and vendor pages). GPU pricing moves weekly with supply, region, and commitment — read this for the shape of the market, then confirm on the provider's own page before you commit a dollar.

- H100 (80GB) — the workhorse, and steady. The cheapest reliable on-demand rate is back near $1.99/hr (Voltage Park), with ~$2.50 PCIe at Hyperstack, ~$2.89 at RunPod, and ~$2.90 SXM at Ori. The median "cheapest across providers" is ~$3.33. Spot dips near $0.94/hr (Prime Intellect). Hyperscaler on-demand: ~$10–13/hr — the same card, 5–6× the money.
- H200 (141GB) — more memory, and firmer than September. Neocloud floors run ~$3.14–3.99/hr (~$3.14 Prime Intellect, ~$3.35 Spheron, ~$3.69 Theta, ~$3.99 Hyperbolic). The Ornn transacted index — settled daily from real neocloud deals — printed $5.24 on Oct 12, and getdeploying's on-demand median is ~$5.00 across 33 providers. Spot ~$2.29. Hyperscaler H200 runs ~$7.91–13.78 (Thunder Compute: AWS ~$7.91–9.89, Azure ~$10.60–13.78).
- B200 (Blackwell, 180GB) — the split-screen card. The cheapest verified in-stock on-demand rate is ~$3.75/hr (Packet.ai, per getdeploying on Oct 22) — essentially flat versus September's ~$3.70. But the on-demand median is now ~$7.99–8.19: RunPod lists $7.99/hr and Together ~$8.19/hr. Spot from ~$3.20 (Vultr). Hyperscaler B200 is ~$14–16/hr.
- GB200 / B300 — the Grace-Blackwell superchips remain premium and partly quote-only: roughly $8/hr and up where published, ~$16–27 at the hyperscalers. If you need one, you're negotiating, not shopping a list.
